heading: CBDT's New Crypto Reporting Guidance: What Investors Need to Know
tldr: The Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) has issued guidance aligning India's crypto reporting with global OECD standards.
This framework focuses on how crypto service providers will collect and share transaction data.
It does not introduce new taxes on crypto assets; existing tax laws remain unchanged.
Accurate and meticulous record-keeping of all crypto transactions is now more crucial than ever for investors.
The guidance facilitates international information exchange, potentially impacting Non-Resident Indian (NRI) investors and those using foreign platforms.
caption:
Heads up, crypto investors! India's tax department has new rules about how crypto platforms will share your transaction details. This isn't about new taxes, but it makes keeping clear records of your buys and sells super important. It also means your crypto activity could be shared internationally. Stay informed and understand what this means for you. Read our full article for details.
